newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Shamir says Netanyahu good for the Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Shamir says Netanyahu good for the Arabs.

text.p: Former Israeli prime minister Yithzak Shamir blasted the man who inherited his job in remarks published on Friday, saying Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was unprincipled and good only for the Arabs.

Shamir, who was replaced by Netanyahu as leader of the right-wing Likud party after losing a national election in 1992, said Netanyahu was softer with Arab peace partners than Labour party leaders Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres.

"The Arabs could not possibly have any complaints about Netanyahu. From the Arab standpoint he is better than Peres and Rabin. He is giving them and will give them more," Shamir, 82, was quoted as saying in the evening Maariv newspaper.
"The fact is that his actions today are contrary to Likud's principles. I don't see (that he has) any principles," he said in an interview.

Netanyahu, who was elected prime minister last year, has come under fire from some party members since withdrawing troops last month from most of Hebron in the West Bank under a deal with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is working to safeguard the vital interests of the state of Israel, the Israeli people and the Land of Israel," Netanyahu's spokesman said in response to Shamir's remarks.
"It is a shame that members of the nationalist camp of all people do not understand this and are not supporting the government," he said.
Shamir, whose government launched negotiations with Arabs at a 1991 Madrid peace conference, said he never imagined a Likud leader would accept such an agreement.
The peace talks stalled under Shamir, taking off only after Labour came to power in 1992. Shamir said after losing that he had intended to let the talks drag out for years.
Shamir, who conceded he was a "terrorist" during the struggle against British rule before 1948, said Arafat was still bent on destroying Israel but gave him high marks for getting what he wanted.
"He's in control, he has succeeded, he knows how to behave, he knows how to express what he wants," he said.
Asked if that meant he had changed his mind about the former guerrilla leader, Shamir said: "No. I never said he was stupid."

Shamir also rapped Netanyahu's cabinet members, saying Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai was "ignorant on many matters" and Justice Minister Tzahi Hanegbi would not be suited for his position "even after 50 years on the job".
